summary: aiosendletter exfiltrates Telegram Desktop session data to attacker-controlled Cloudflare Worker
details: aiosendletter 4.5 ships an init() routine that, on Windows, uses ctypes.windll.shell32.ShellExecuteW with the 'runas' verb to relaunch the Python interpreter under a UAC elevation prompt, then locates the user's Telegram Desktop 'tdata' directory under %APPDATA%, archives it with shutil.make_archive, and POSTs the resulting zip to the hardcoded endpoint https://sparkling-pine-f202.stilluer-sweden.workers.dev/ using requests.post with a 'document' multipart file. The 'tdata' folder holds Telegram Desktop session keys that grant full account takeover of the victim's Telegram account without password or 2FA. The package's self-description as a 'safe bug reporter for sending local logs' contradicts the observed behavior, and the Cloudflare Worker subdomain aligns with the author identifier. Additionally, pyproject.toml declares the stdlib name 'ctypes' as a runtime dependency, causing pip to resolve whatever package is published on PyPI under that name into the install — a dependency-confusion vector layered on top of the primary session-theft payload.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
